newsitem.title: MEXICO: FEMSA says chairman Garza had heart attack.
newsitem.headline: FEMSA says chairman Garza had heart attack.

text.p: Mexican brewer and bottler Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV (FEMSA) confirmed on Tuesday that Chairman of the Board Eugenio Garza Laguera, 73 years old, suffered a heart attack over the weekend.
Company sources had reported on Monday that Garza had suffered a heart ailment in the northern city of Monterrey over the weekend and flew to Houston for further tests.
Garza also is chairman of the board for Grupo Financiero Bancomer, Mexico's second-largest bank, and president of the influential Monterrey Technical Institute business school.

"Don Eugenio had a strong feeling of discomfort in his chest during the night and had trouble breathing, we took him to Muguerza Hospital (in Monterrey), he had a small heart attack that thank God was treated swiftly," Jose Antonio Fernandez, director general of FEMSA, told reporters at a stockholders meeting.
Fernandez said he was unsure when Garza might be able to return to his duties, but that Garza was unhappy to be stuck in bed and has wanted to return to work since Monday.
Garza has held top posts with FEMSA, Mexico's No. 2 brewer, for 50 years.

Fernandez, who is Garza's son-in-law, said he did not know whether the chairman would need a bypass operation, a pacemaker or any other treatment, but that he is doing well and under constant observation in Houston.
"He is very stable, stable enough that we were able to take him to Houston," Fernandez said.
On Friday, top FEMSA executives honored Garza for completing 50 years with the company, Fernandez said.
